title: Evercraft College Football Power Rankings: Alabama Leads the Field
dek: Our results-first model ranks all FBS programs from completed NCAA game evidence through October 7, 2026, with opponent strength, capped scoring margins, venue, recent form and uncertainty kept visible.

claims.claim: The ranking evidence ledger contains 393 completed games through 2026-10-07.
Alabama ranks No. 1 in Evercraft CFBPI run cfbpi:cd08f777eee25c5c5dc3a1b6, ahead of Notre Dame.

sections.heading: What the model sees right now
sections.body: The first five positions in this edition are #1 Alabama, #2 Notre Dame, #3 Texas, #4 Texas Tech, #5 Indiana. This is not a ballot and it is not designed to copy one. The ordering comes from the season ledger attached to ranking run cfbpi:cd08f777eee25c5c5dc3a1b6. Completed results are adjusted for opponent strength and designated venue, scoring margins are capped so one demolition cannot own an entire résumé, and the most recent games matter without erasing the rest of the season. The top line is therefore a snapshot of demonstrated team strength through the evidence cutoff, not a prediction that the current order will survive the next Saturday.

sections.heading: Movement since the last edition
sections.body: Risers: Utah up 1 to No. 7; Florida up 1 to No. 23. Fallers: Georgia down 1 to No. 8; James Madison down 1 to No. 24. Movement is computed against the latest strictly earlier persisted Evercraft edition, so a rerun of the same evidence window cannot manufacture a new arrow.

sections.heading: Why Alabama is No. 1
sections.body: Alabama is 5-0 and owns a Power Score of 81.40 with 95 percent model confidence. Its current component profile combines a result-quality score of 80.8, opponent-adjusted efficiency of 91.5, schedule strength of 62.1 and recent-form score of 81.0. The important part is not any single number. The lead survives several independent pieces of the current results ledger rather than depending on poll reputation or one headline win.

sections.heading: Where uncertainty still lives
sections.body: This edition deliberately leaves availability and turnover-sustainability inputs unfilled when they are not backed by a governed evidence feed. Missing information is not converted into zero and modeled values are not labeled as observations. Every team therefore carries an explicit confidence value and a missing-component list in the machine-readable ranking receipt. That makes this edition more conservative than a ranking that quietly guesses at injuries, quarterback availability or turnover luck, and it gives future versions a clean place to improve as those evidence lanes become reliable.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.body: The ranking is designed to move when the evidence moves. Each new completed-game ledger can be replayed against the same versioned model, compared with the prior published edition and scored later against what happened on the field. Verified player availability and deeper efficiency measures can be added as governed evidence lanes without rewriting history. The comparison and accountability ledgers preserve where Evercraft disagreed with consensus and whether those directional calls held up later. The goal is not to win an argument on publication day. It is to build a public record showing where Evercraft was early, where it was wrong and whether the model becomes more predictive as the season develops.

uncertainty_notes: Player availability is not yet included unless a governed evidence feed is added.
Turnover sustainability is intentionally missing in this edition rather than inferred.
NCAA scoreboard data may designate home and away without exposing neutral-site state for every game.
This is a power ranking derived from completed results, not a playoff selection projection.

derivatives.copy: The Evercraft College Football Power Rankings are live for 2026-10-07. Alabama is No. 1, but the bigger story is the method: completed results, opponent strength, capped margins and visible uncertainty instead of a copied ballot.

We built our college football power ranking as a replayable evidence product rather than a one-off opinion list. Every position traces back to the same completed-game ledger and versioned model, with missing inputs left missing instead of silently guessed.

derivatives.hook: Alabama is No. 1 in Evercraft College Football Power Rankings. Here are the five teams our results model trusts most right now.
